key.name: wrap-around
key.description: Switching past the last workspace on a secondary monitor returns to the first, and switching before the first goes to the last. The primary monitor always stops at either end, as GNOME itself does: it drives the real workspace, and wrapping it would slide backwards across every workspace to get there.

key.name: animation-duration
key.description: How long a workspace slide takes. The default matches GNOME's own workspace switch. Swipes are scaled by this rather than fixed to it, so a fast flick stays fast.

key.name: debug-logging
key.summary: Write detailed logs to the journal
key.description: Records every workspace switch and every window this extension moves. Off by default, and deliberately not shown in the preferences window: it is for diagnosing a problem, not for daily use. Turn it on with gsettings, reproduce the problem, then read the journal with journalctl -f -o cat /usr/bin/gnome-shell.
